info.title: TelltaleDNS API
info.description: Read and control a TelltaleDNS resolver. JSON is camelCase; field names carry units (`totalMs`, `ttlSeconds`). Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json with a stable `code` and a `hint`. Time parameters take RFC 3339 or a relative offset (`-24h`). Collections page with `cursor`/`limit`. Analytics calls take `scope` (`cluster` or `node:local`; both mean this node until clustering is available).

get.summary: Device anomalies: rate spikes, heavy volume to one domain, drift, beaconing (OBS-013).
get.description:
Each finding compares a device with its own learned baseline (after a learning period,
7 days by default) and carries the evidence: observed value, usual value ± spread, the
threshold, and the window. Findings are alert-only; TelltaleDNS never blocks on them.
Newest first.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only findings whose window started after this (RFC 3339 or relative, default `-7d`).

get.description:
Every change to users, passwords, two-factor sign-in, and API tokens, sign-ins and
lockouts, and configuration reloads, newest first, with who (attributed to the token and
its owner for API tokens), from where, why (`X-Telltale-Reason`), and what changed. Append-only and
hash-chained; check it with GET /audit/verify.

Recomputes every entry's hash and link. `ok: false` with `firstBadSeq` means the log was
edited at or before that entry outside TelltaleDNS. Compare `headHash` with a value you
saved earlier to detect removed entries at the end.

post.description:
Username and password, plus `totp` (or `recoveryCode`) when two-factor sign-in is on:
without it the answer is 401 `totp_required`. Sets an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` session
cookie and returns the CSRF token to send as `X-CSRF-Token` on changes. Repeated failures
lock the username and the address out for a while (429).
Ends this session and clears the cookie. With a token or Basic, does nothing but succeed.

200.description: Signed out of an OIDC session: send the browser to `logoutUrl` to sign out at the provider too.

get.description:
The signed-in user: role (capped by a token's scope), two-factor state, unused recovery
codes, and how this request authenticated.

The provider returns here with `code` and `state`. Validates both, exchanges the code,
verifies the ID token, maps groups to a role (creating the user on first sign-in), sets
the session cookie, and redirects to the UI. Failures redirect to `/#/?loginError=...`.
Register `<public_url>/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/callback` with the provider.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set instead of `code` when the user cancelled or the provider refused.

302.description: Signed in (to the UI), or back to sign-in with `loginError`.

get.summary: Start signing in with an OIDC provider.
get.description:
Redirects the browser to the provider (Authorization Code + PKCE). The provider sends it
back to `/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/callback`, which signs in and returns to `returnTo`.
Browsers only: link a "Sign in with ..." button here.

parameters.name: returnTo
parameters.description: UI route to return to after sign-in (`/#/queries`). Default `/#/`.

post.description: Needs the current password. Ends every other session of this user.

Only while no user exists. `setupToken` is printed in the server log at startup and saved
in `<data_dir>/setup-token`. Signs the new admin in (sets the session cookie).

get.description:
Whether first-run setup is needed, and who the request is signed in as (if anyone),
with the session's CSRF token. Public; the UI calls it on load.

post.description: Needs the current password. Removes the TOTP secret and the unused recovery codes.

Confirms a current code from the app enrolled with POST /auth/totp/setup, turns
enforcement on, and returns ten single-use recovery codes (shown only now).

Returns a new TOTP secret (base32 and an `otpauth://` URL for a QR code). Nothing is
enforced until POST /auth/totp/enable confirms a code from the app.

get.summary: Download a backup of this node.
get.description:
One `.ttbk` file (ADR-063) with the configuration files, users and API tokens, devices and
names made through the API, the audit log, statistics history, and anomaly baselines.
Sign-in sessions, lists, and the cluster identity aren't included, and neither is the
query log (use `telltale backup create --include-qlog` for that). Restore it with
`telltale backup restore FILE` on the new machine.

The file holds password hashes: keep it private. Admin only; audited as `backup.create`.

200.description: The backup, as an attachment named `telltale-<node>-<time>.ttbk`.

503.description: Backups aren't available on this node.

get.summary: Configured clients (devices) and how they're recognized.
get.description:
Each device's name, the IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or client IDs that identify it, and its groups in
priority order (the first group's settings apply). Unknown devices use the `default` group.

put.summary: Create, rename, or change a device (API-010).
put.description:
Names devices across every view: the query log, live tail, charts, and history (names
are resolved when read, so earlier queries are relabelled too). To rename, send the new
`name` in the body. Devices defined in the config files are read-only here (409). Needs
the operator role (or a `write` token).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The device's current name (or the name for a new one).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

409.description: Defined in the config files, or an Idempotency-Key reused for another request.

412.description: If-Match: the config changed since that version.

422.description: The resulting configuration is invalid (e.g. an unknown group).

delete.summary: Delete a device named through the API.
delete.description:
Its queries, past and future, go back to showing the address, and it leaves its groups
(the `default` group applies). Devices from the config files can't be deleted here (409).
Needs the operator role (or a `write` token).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

404.description: No device by that name was created through the API.

get.description:
Every node this node knows: role, link state and round-trip time, configuration version
and lag, and whether it's serving DNS (queries per second, SERVFAIL share, upstream p90).
Plus `checks` (each with a plain-language fix when failing) and recent `events`. On a
standalone node, `enabled` is false. Use it to answer "is the cluster healthy and serving?".

post.description:
Manual failover (ADR-051): use when the primary is gone. The node takes a new epoch,
publishes the cluster's configuration from the last version it applied, and every node
follows it. An old primary that comes back steps down, and anything it changed meanwhile
shows under `conflicts`.

Refused when:
- the current primary is up;
- the node isn't eligible or lacks the cluster key;
- without `emergency`, the cluster takes its configuration from Git and this node isn't
  managed from Git.

Admin only; audited as `cluster.promote`.

200.description: Promoted; the cluster as it is now.

409.description: Not allowed now (the primary is up, or this node can't be primary).

get.description:
Why `name` is or isn't blocked for a client: how the client is identified, its groups,
every matching rule in every list (with the list line), which rule decides, and where the
query would be forwarded. Example: `GET /api/v1/explain?name=ads.example.com&client=192.168.1.20`.

parameters.name: mac
parameters.description: The client's MAC address (default: from the neighbor table).

get.summary: Domains sent to other DNS servers (conditional forwarding).
get.description:
Each domain whose names are asked of specific servers instead of the public upstreams,
with where it's defined (`file` or `api`). The `ETag` is the config version for `If-Match`.

put.summary: Send a domain to other DNS servers (conditional forwarding; API-011).
put.description:
Every name under `domain` is asked of `servers` (in order, failing over) instead of the
public upstreams: a work network's DNS over a VPN, a router that knows your devices, another
lab. A bare address means plain DNS; `tls://` and `https://` URLs work too. Local names still
answer first. Domains routed in the config files are read-only here (409).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The domain, e.g. corp.example (its whole subtree is sent).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

422.description: A server isn't an address or a supported URL.

delete.summary: Stop sending a domain to other servers.
delete.description:
Names under it go to the public upstreams again. Routes from the config files can't be
removed here (409).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

get.summary: Client groups, their lists, block mode, and pause state.
get.description:
Groups decide which lists apply to a device and how blocked queries are answered. `lists`
null means every enabled list; `pausedUntilUnixSeconds` is set while blocking is paused.

post.description:
Point the repository's push webhook here (content type JSON, with the secret from
`[cluster.git] webhook_secret_file`): the primary checks the ref at once instead of at
the next poll. Authenticated by the `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC, not a session.

202.description: The ref will be checked now.

get.summary: Filter lists and their download state.
get.description:
Every configured list with its kind (block/allow), source, download state (`ok`, `failed`,
`pending`) and last error, size, and how many names it contributes to the active snapshot.

Newest first. Filters combine with AND: name (substring by default; `match=exact|suffix|
glob|regex`), client, status, query type, response code, upstream, minimum latency, and
time range. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for older rows. Example:
`GET /api/v1/queries?name=doubleclick&status=blocked&from=-1h&limit=50`.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only queries from devices in this group (a group name, ADR-050).

parameters.name: minLatencyMs
parameters.description: Only queries that took at least this long.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start: RFC 3339 or relative (`-1h`). Default: no limit.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continue after a previous page (`nextCursor` from it).

get.description:
Server-Sent Events, newest as they happen: `event: query` carries a `QueryRow` (same
fields as GET /queries), `event: dropped` a `TailDropped` when matching queries were
skipped (over `rate`, or this client fell behind), and a comment every 15 s keeps the
connection open. Filters are applied on the server. In a browser:
`new EventSource('/api/v1/queries/stream?status=blocked')` (the session cookie signs it
in). Honors the query-log privacy level; at most 16 streams per node.

parameters.name: minLatencyMs
parameters.description: Only queries that took at least this long.

parameters.name: rate
parameters.description:
Most events per second sent to this subscriber (1–2000, default 500). The rest are
counted and reported in `dropped` events.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `cluster` (default) or `node:local`. The live stream is always this node's queries.

get.summary: Names on my network: the names TelltaleDNS answers itself.
get.description:
Every local name with its records and where it's defined (`file`: read-only here; `api`:
editable with `PUT /records/{name}`). The `ETag` is the config version for `If-Match`.

put.summary: Set a local name's records (API-011, "Names on my network").
put.description:
Replaces every record of `name` made through the API with `records` (A and AAAA addresses,
CNAME aliases, and in Advanced PTR, TXT, MX, SRV). TelltaleDNS then answers the name itself,
before the cache and upstreams; reverse lookups for addresses are added automatically
(`[local] auto_ptr`). Names defined in the config files are read-only here (409). Needs the
operator role (or a `write` token).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The full name, e.g. nas.home.arpa (a leading `*.` makes a wildcard).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

409.description: Defined in the config files, or an Idempotency-Key reused.

422.description: A value doesn't fit its type (e.g. A with a name), or the result is invalid.

delete.summary: Remove a local name made through the API.
delete.description:
TelltaleDNS stops answering it itself; queries for it go to the upstreams (or a route) as
usual. Names from the config files can't be removed here (409).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

404.description: No name like that was created through the API.

get.description:
By answer path and transport, query type, upstream server, or the upstream stage, for the
current or previous hour, in milliseconds (HDR histograms, 2 significant digits).

Queries, blocked (count and percent), cache hits, forwarded, NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL counts
over the range (per-minute data up to 48 hours back, hourly rollups beyond), plus this
hour's active clients and latency percentiles by answer path. Example:
`GET /api/v1/stats/summary?from=-24h` or `?from=-30d`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Start: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`, `-30d`). Default: 24 hours ago. Ranges over
48 hours are summed from hourly rollups.

get.description:
Buckets by status, query type, and response code, plus upstream exchanges. `step=second`
covers the last 15 minutes, `step=minute` 7 days (48 hours live), `step=hour` 400 days,
`step=day` everything. Buckets without queries are omitted. Example:
`GET /api/v1/stats/timeseries?from=-30d&step=hour`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Start: RFC 3339 or relative (`-1h`). Default: 5 minutes ago (second steps), 1 hour
(minute), 7 days (hour), or 90 days (day).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End: RFC 3339 or relative. Default: now.

get.summary: Top domains, blocked domains, NXDOMAIN names, or clients.
get.description:
Ranked by a Space-Saving sketch per hour: `count` is an upper bound and `errorBound` how
far it may be over. Example: `GET /api/v1/stats/top?kind=blocked&limit=10`. With
`kind=domains&client=192.168.1.20`, one client's top domains (recently active clients only).

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Only this client's domains (an IP address; `kind=domains` only).

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only this group's queries (a group name; not with `client`, not for `nxdomain`).

get.description:
Version, role, uptime, listeners, whether the query log is on, and the active filter
snapshot. Cheap; suitable for health dashboards.
Name, scope, expiry, and last use. The secrets themselves are never shown again.

post.description:
For scripts, dashboards, and agents: send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. `scope`
`read` acts as viewer, `write` as operator, `admin` as admin, never above the owner's role.
The token is shown only in this response.

delete.summary: Revoke one of my API tokens.
delete.description: By the `id` from GET /tokens. Takes effect immediately; other tokens are unaffected.

get.summary: Upstream servers with health and latency.
get.description:
Every upstream with its stable ID, endpoint, groups, circuit-breaker state (`closed` means
healthy), request and failure counts, and smoothed answer time in milliseconds.
Every user with role, status, and two-factor state.

post.description: `role` is `viewer`, `operator`, or `admin`. The password needs at least 10 characters.

delete.description: Also deletes their sessions and tokens. The last enabled admin can't be deleted.

patch.description:
Role, disabled, HTTP Basic opt-in, a new password (ends their sessions), or a TOTP reset.
The last enabled admin can't be demoted or disabled.

AnomalyFinding.description: A device anomaly and its evidence (OBS-013). Alert-only: TelltaleDNS never acts on it.

client.description: The device's address, and its name when known.

detail.description: The finding in words, with the numbers.

domain.description: The registrable domain, for domain findings.

observed.description: What was seen, the device's usual value (± spread), and the bar it crossed.

windowStart.description: The window examined (RFC 3339 start, and length in seconds).

actor.description:
A username, `token:<name> (owner: <user>)`, or a system name (`setup-token`,
`bootstrap`, `lockout`, `reload`).

detail.description: Details (what changed, as `{field: {from, to}}` for updates). Never secrets.

hash.description: BLAKE3 of the previous entry's hash and this entry (hex).

AuditPage.description: A page of the audit log, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for older entries; absent at the start of the log.

AuditVerify.description: Result of checking the hash chain.

firstBadSeq.description: The first entry that was changed, removed, or reordered.

headHash.description: Hash of the newest entry (hex). Record it elsewhere to detect truncation later.

ok.description: Every entry's hash and link checks out.

AuthStatus.description: Whether setup is needed and who is signed in (public).

csrfToken.description: For session sign-ins: send as `X-CSRF-Token` on changes.

localLogin.description:
Password sign-in is offered to this client (off with `disable_local_login`, except
from the break-glass admin networks).

oidc.description: OIDC providers: send the browser to `GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/start`.

setupRequired.description: No user exists yet: create the first admin with the setup token.

ClientChange.description: What a device change did, or would do with `dryRun=true` (AGT-002).

oneOf.description: The device after the change (absent after a delete).
The device before the change (absent when it's new).

configVersion.description: The configuration version after the change (send it as `If-Match` next time).

recentQueries.description:
Queries in the current and previous hour from the addresses it matches: how much
history gets the new label (names are resolved when read, so the past is relabelled).

effectiveGroups.description:
The groups that actually apply, highest priority first: `groups` when set, else the
group of the network its addresses are in (ADR-050), else the default group. Empty
when it depends on the address it's seen at (a device known only by MAC).

match.description: IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or `id:<client-id>` this device is recognized by.

source.description:
`file` (defined in the config files: read-only here) or `api` (named in the UI or
through the API: editable with `PUT /clients/{name}`).

ClientInput.description: A device to create, rename, or change (`PUT /api/v1/clients/{name}`, API-010).

match.description: How to recognize it: IPs, CIDRs, MACs (`aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`), or `id:<client-id>`.

name.description: The new name, to rename the device (default: the name in the path).

ClusterCheck.description: One health check with a plain-language fix when it fails.

fix.description: What to do about it (failing checks only).

ClusterConflict.description:
A version an old primary published after a newer primary took over: never applied
anywhere; listed so the change can be re-made on the current primary.

changed.description: Settings that differ from the current primary's version (dotted paths).

detectedAt.description: When the newer primary's version arrived (RFC 3339).

ClusterEvent.description: A cluster event (joins, connections, published and applied versions, failures).

ClusterFailover.description: Automatic failover as this node sees it (ADR-056).

active.description: Whether elections run: `auto`, with three or more voters, this node one of them.

leaseHeld.description: This node is the elected primary and its lease holds.

leaseSecondsLeft.description: How long its lease still runs, in seconds (primaries only).

reachableVoters.description: Voters this node has a stream to (itself included).

votedEpoch.description: The epoch and node this node last voted for.

ClusterInfo.description: This node's cluster membership and the peers it holds a stream with.

certExpiresAt.description: When this node's cluster certificate expires (RFC 3339).

configCreatedAt.description: When that version was created on the primary (RFC 3339).

configSeq.description: The configuration version this node published (primary) or applied (replica), CLU-003.

lastSyncFetched.description: Blobs fetched for the last applied version (replicas).

lastSyncMs.description: Fetch + apply time of the last sync, in milliseconds.

name.description: The name given at `telltale cluster init`.

nodeId.description: This node's ID (from its key; stable across restarts).

peers.description: Peers this node has heard from since it started.

primary.description: Whether this node holds the cluster CA (the first node, until promotion arrives).

syncError.description: The last replication error, until the next success.

behindSeconds.description: How long it has been behind (absent when in sync).

certExpiresAt.description: This node only: when its cluster certificate expires (RFC 3339).

configSource.description: How the node's own configuration is managed: `gitops` or `file` (ADR-048).

connected.description: A stream to it is open (this node: n/a, true).

ephemeral.description: A Kubernetes resolver pod (CLU-009): dropped when no longer heard from.

protocol.description: The cluster protocol it speaks (CLU-010); nodes within one version work together.

qps.description: Queries per second over the last minute.

ready.description: Serving DNS (listeners bound, not shutting down).

rttMs.description: Round-trip time over the cluster link.

servfailPercent.description: SERVFAIL share over the last minute, percent.

sourceCommit.description: The Git commit of the configuration it serves (ADR-049).

up.description: Heard from within 15 s (always true for this node).

ClusterPeer.description: A peer node, as last heard over the cluster channel.

configSeq.description: The configuration version the peer reports as applied (the primary: published).

up.description: Heard from within the last three heartbeats (15 s).

ClusterSource.description: The cluster's configuration from Git (ADR-049): the commit in use and the last check.

checkedAt.description: When the primary last checked the ref (RFC 3339; on the primary only).

commit.description: The commit every node should be serving.

error.description: Why the last check failed, or why the newest commit was refused.

refused.description:
The newest commit isn't acceptable (invalid, unsigned, rewound): the cluster stays on
`commit`.

signedBy.description: The allowed signer who signed it (with `require_signed`).

ClusterView.description:
The cluster as this node sees it (REQ: CLU-008): every node with its health, sync, and
serving state, a timeline, and a pass/fail check list.

authority.description: Where the cluster's configuration comes from: `api` or `gitops` (ADR-048).

conflicts.description: Versions this node published that the cluster moved on without (ADR-051), newest first.

enabled.description: False on a standalone node (everything else is then empty).

newestConfigSeq.description: The newest configuration version any node reports.

nodes.description: This node first, then peers by site and ID.

oneOf.description: The Git repository the configuration comes from, when it does (ADR-049).

ConfigChange.description: What a change to local names or forwarded domains did (or would do, with `dryRun`).

after.description: The entry after (absent after a delete).

configVersion.description: The configuration version after the change (send it as `If-Match` next time).

allowBasicApi.description: Allow HTTP Basic on the API for scripts and scrapers (default false).

device.description: The configured device it was recognized as.

routed.description: An explicit route matched (not just the default group).

enabled.description: The client's groups use this list.

lines.description: Where the rule is in the list.

Explanation.description: Why a name is or isn't blocked for a client, and where it would go (FLT-013).

oneOf.description: Every matching rule in precedence order; absent until a filter is loaded.

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this client until then (Unix seconds).

ForwardInfo.description: A domain sent to other servers (conditional forwarding).

ForwardInput.description: The servers a domain is sent to (`PUT /api/v1/forwards/{domain}`).

servers.description: Addresses (plain DNS) or `udp://`, `tcp://`, `tls://`, `https://` URLs, tried in order.

color.description: `#rrggbb` for charts and chips (configured, or a stable pick).

devicesThisHour.description: Devices seen in the group this hour.

lists.description: Lists this group uses; null means every enabled list.

networks.description: Networks (CIDRs) whose devices belong to this group (ADR-050).

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this group until then (Unix seconds).

queries24h.description: Queries from the group's devices over the last 24 hours.

Hour.description: Which hour a top-K or latency call reads.

Items_AnomalyFinding.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: A device anomaly and its evidence (OBS-013). Alert-only: TelltaleDNS never acts on it.

client.description: The device's address, and its name when known.

detail.description: The finding in words, with the numbers.

domain.description: The registrable domain, for domain findings.

observed.description: What was seen, the device's usual value (± spread), and the bar it crossed.

windowStart.description: The window examined (RFC 3339 start, and length in seconds).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_ClientInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

effectiveGroups.description:
The groups that actually apply, highest priority first: `groups` when set, else the
group of the network its addresses are in (ADR-050), else the default group. Empty
when it depends on the address it's seen at (a device known only by MAC).

match.description: IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or `id:<client-id>` this device is recognized by.

source.description:
`file` (defined in the config files: read-only here) or `api` (named in the UI or
through the API: editable with `PUT /clients/{name}`).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_ForwardInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: A domain sent to other servers (conditional forwarding).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_GroupInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

color.description: `#rrggbb` for charts and chips (configured, or a stable pick).

devicesThisHour.description: Devices seen in the group this hour.

lists.description: Lists this group uses; null means every enabled list.

networks.description: Networks (CIDRs) whose devices belong to this group (ADR-050).

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this group until then (Unix seconds).

queries24h.description: Queries from the group's devices over the last 24 hours.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_LatencyRow.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: Latency percentiles for one key (HDR histogram, 2 significant digits).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_ListInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: A filter list and its download state.

entries.description: Names this list contributes to the active snapshot.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_LocalName.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_TimeBucket.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

byGroup.description: Queries by the client's group (ADR-050). Empty for buckets read from rollups.

upstreamQueries.description: Upstream exchanges, and how many failed.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_TopItem.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description:
One ranked item. Counts come from a Space-Saving sketch: the true count lies in
`[count - errorBound, count]`.

groups.description:
For clients: the groups whose settings apply to it, highest priority first (its
device's groups, else its network's group, else the default; ADR-050).

name.description: The configured device name, for clients that have one.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_UpstreamInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: An upstream server and its health.

id.description: Stable ID (config order, from 1); query rows and latency rows refer to it.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

LatencyRow.description: Latency percentiles for one key (HDR histogram, 2 significant digits).

ListInfo.description: A filter list and its download state.

entries.description: Names this list contributes to the active snapshot.

oidcProvider.description: The sign-in provider for users created by OIDC sign-in (they have no password here).

totp.description: 6-digit code from the authenticator app, when TOTP is on.

csrfToken.description: Send as `X-CSRF-Token` on every change made with this session.

logoutUrl.description: Send the browser here to also sign out at the provider.

MaskedClients.description: Evidence that client IPs appear masked.

sharePercent.description: Share of the window's queries sent by `sources`, in percent (> 90).

sources.description: The infrastructure addresses that sent them, heaviest first (at most 3).

recoveryCodesLeft.description: Unused recovery codes (when TOTP is on).

role.description: Effective role (a token's scope caps its owner's role).

token.description: The token, shown only now: send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

detail.description: What went wrong in this request.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

example.detail: `from`: `yesterday`: expected RFC 3339 time (2026-10-03T12:00:00Z) or a relative offset (-24h)
example.hint: Use a relative offset such as -24h, or RFC 3339 such as 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z.
example.title: Invalid parameter

emergency.description:
Promote even though this node can't publish configuration under the cluster's
authority (configuration from Git, and no Git-managed node reachable): it coordinates the
cluster and keeps the last version, and publishes nothing new (ADR-048).

QueryPage.description: A page of query-log rows, newest first.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read (CLU-002: partial results, never a hang).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get older rows; absent when there are none.

scanned.description: How much of the log this page looked at.

clientName.description: The configured device name, when known.

list.description: The list whose rule blocked or allowed the query.

node.description: The node that answered it (federated reads: its site).

rcode.description: Response code, or null when nothing was sent.

RecordInput.description: One record of a local name.

value.description:
An address for A/AAAA, a name for CNAME/PTR, text for TXT, `"10 mail.home.arpa"` for MX,
`"0 5 5060 pbx.home.arpa"` for SRV.

Scope.description: An API token's scope; a token never exceeds its owner's role.

cacheHitPercent.description: Cache share of answered queries that weren't blocked or local, 0–100.

latency.description: Latency percentiles this hour, by answer path (`cache`, `upstream`, ...).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read (CLU-002).

oneOf.description:
Present when client IPs appear masked (OPS-003): most recent queries come from a few
infrastructure addresses (a Kubernetes node, a Docker bridge, a forwarding router),
so per-device statistics and rules see those instead of devices.
Present when this node belongs to a cluster (CLU-001).

filterNames.description: Blocked names in the active snapshot.

filterSnapshot.description: Version of the active filter snapshot, if one is loaded.

queryLog.description: Whether the per-query log is being written.

TailDropped.description: Sent as an SSE `dropped` event when matching queries weren't delivered.

dropped.description: How many matching queries were skipped since the last report.

reason.description: `rate`: over this subscriber's `rate`; `lag`: the subscriber fell behind.

byGroup.description: Queries by the client's group (ADR-050). Empty for buckets read from rollups.

upstreamQueries.description: Upstream exchanges, and how many failed.

TopItem.description:
One ranked item. Counts come from a Space-Saving sketch: the true count lies in
`[count - errorBound, count]`.

groups.description:
For clients: the groups whose settings apply to it, highest priority first (its
device's groups, else its network's group, else the default; ADR-050).

name.description: The configured device name, for clients that have one.

secretBase32.description: For manual entry in an authenticator app.

password.description: Set a new password (ends the user's sessions).

resetTotp.description: Turn off the user's TOTP (if they lost their device).

UpstreamInfo.description: An upstream server and its health.

id.description: Stable ID (config order, from 1); query rows and latency rows refer to it.

oidcProvider.description: The sign-in provider for users created by OIDC sign-in (they have no password here).

tags.name: stats
tags.description: Counters, top lists, and latency percentiles. Live windows in memory (15 minutes per second, 48 hours per minute) plus rollups on disk (7 days per minute, 400 days per hour, days forever).

tags.name: queries
tags.description: The query log and explanations of decisions.

tags.name: config
tags.description: Lists, groups, clients, and upstreams as running.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, two-factor, API tokens, and users. Everything else needs one of: the session cookie from POST /auth/login (plus X-CSRF-Token on changes), Authorization: Bearer <token>, or HTTP Basic for users who allow it.
